title: Wendell and the Wolf
premise: Mara Halloran, a temple scribe bound by debt to the valley where magic cannot follow, discovers that Wendell — the quiet wolf-keeper she has loved for years — carries a stolen soul and the gift the crown has outlawed. When royal hunters breach the valley, the two flee into a world of fading enchantment, pursued by a court beneath the mountain that buys souls to fuel its endless winter. To save them both, Mara must trade her own memories, piece by piece, until she risks forgetting why she ever loved him. In the end, Wendell returns her sold soul to the court at terrible cost, and Mara wakes in the valley with no memory of him — except a wolf who refuses to leave, waiting for love to remember itself.
about_author: Ines Ishikawa is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters never meant to be read, an experience that taught her how memory and devotion entangle. She writes fantasy about ordinary people caught in machinery far larger than themselves, and lives near a forest she refuses to enter after dark.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Introduces the debt-bound temple, the valley's magic-dead borders, and Mara's careful, small life copying ledgers. She notices Wendell, the wolf-keeper, watching the border stones as if listening to something beyond them. Emotional beat: restless longing disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: Ink and Ash
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A royal proclamation arrives: all gifted persons must be surrendered for the hunt. The temple elders comply eagerly, trading names against their own debts. Mara realizes her name is on a list she herself was made to copy. Emotional beat: dread and complicity.

chapters.title: What the Wolves Keep
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Revealed: he is gifted, hiding in the only place magic cannot find him, guarding a soul vial stolen from the mountain court years ago. The wolves are his sentries. He knows the hunt is coming and prepares to run alone. Emotional beat: guilt and isolation.

chapters.title: Hunters at the Gate
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Royal hunters arrive with a soul-sniffing hound. Wendell is betrayed by a temple elder. In the chaos, Mara burns the ledger bearing his name — damning herself — and flees with him through the border stones. Emotional beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: Crossing Into Color
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Beyond the valley, magic floods back: singing rivers, predatory light. Mara experiences wonder and terror; Wendell teaches her the rules of a gifted world. First tenderness between them. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by fear.

chapters.title: The Road of Sold Names
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. They travel toward the mountain court, following rumors of a market where souls are traded. They pass villages emptied by the hunt. Mara learns what Wendell's stolen soul is: it belongs to his sister, taken as payment for his life. Emotional beat: grief reframing love.

chapters.title: A Fair of Small Magics
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A hidden market of fugitive gifteds. They seek a guide to the under-mountain road but attract attention from a broker named Sef, who recognizes the soul vial and covets it. Emotional beat: fragile community, new threat.

chapters.title: Sef's Bargain
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Sef offers passage in exchange for a memory of Mara's choosing — the court pays handsomely for memories of love. Wendell forbids it; Mara secretly considers it, learning the price of the road ahead. Emotional beat: temptation and first real conflict between them.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Begins
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The first snows fall unnaturally early — the court beneath the mountain is feeding winter to extend its power. Fugitives freeze mid-flight. Wendell uses his gift openly for the first time to save a child, exposing them both. Emotional beat: sacrifice hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Fair
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Hunters raze the fair; Sef sells their location to buy his own safety. Mara and Wendell escape into the high passes with nothing but the vial and each other. Emotional beat: loss, betrayal, and stubborn survival.

chapters.title: What I Would Give
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Sheltered in a cave, Wendell confesses everything: the sister, the theft, the debt that started the hunt. Mara confesses she would trade her memories to finish the journey. They argue, then hold each other in the dark. Emotional beat: love stated plainly at last.

chapters.title: The Under-Mountain Road
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Guided by wolves who refuse to leave Wendell, they descend through abandoned mine-shafts lit by trapped souls. The walls whisper with voices of the sold. Mara begins hearing her mother among them — a lie planted by the mountain. Emotional beat: haunting, disorientation.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. They reach the court: a glittering hall where the Winter Regent wears bought memories like jewels. Wendell offers himself in exchange for his sister's soul. The Regent counters: he wants Mara's memories of love instead — they burn brightest. Emotional beat: horror dressed in beauty.

chapters.title: Chains of Debt
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Imprisoned in the guest-wing-that-is-a-cage, Mara meets Wendell's sister, hollowed and gentle, who doesn't remember him. Mara sees her own possible future. She begins quietly stealing keys with borrowed magic. Emotional beat: empathy sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Regent's Gift
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The Regent shows Wendell the truth: the hunt was engineered to harvest gifteds, and Wendell's old theft was permitted — bait to draw stronger souls down. His rebellion was always part of the machine. Emotional beat: despair, the corruption of power laid bare.

chapters.title: A Memory Spent
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. To free Wendell, Mara trades one memory of him to a sympathetic servant — the day they met. She feels the hole where it was and chooses to keep going anyway. Emotional beat: heartbreak as deliberate cost.

chapters.title: The Soul Ledger
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Using her scribe's training, Mara finds the court's master ledger — every soul and memory recorded, including the Regent's own original name and sold self. Knowledge becomes leverage. Emotional beat: the powerless turning paperwork into a weapon.

chapters.title: Winter's Heart
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Confrontation in the Regent's hall. Wendell shatters the soul-vats while Mara reads the Regent's true name from the ledger, unraveling his borrowed power. The false winter breaks; the mountain begins to wake. Emotional beat: climax — fury, terror, triumph.

chapters.title: The Price of Names
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The collapsing court demands a soul to seal its waking. Wendell gives his own — not to the Regent, but to the mountain itself, buying every captive's freedom including his sister's and Mara's. He fades in Mara's arms, asking her to forget him gently. Emotional beat: devastating sacrifice.

chapters.title: Exodus
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara leads the freed captives up through the thawing mines, carrying Wendell's sister and a vial of snow that hums faintly — the last trace of him. The valley border stones crack as magic returns to the world. Emotional beat: mourning braided with hope.

chapters.title: The Wolf Who Waited
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, epilogue-tone. Seasons later, Mara runs the temple archive, freed of debt, her memories scarred but intact. A grey wolf appears at the valley edge and will not leave. Slowly, impossibly, fragments return — warmth, ink, a name half-spoken. Emotional beat: love outlasting memory.

chapters.title: Wendell and the Wolf
chapters.summary: Dual POV finale. The mountain, paid in full, returns what it took: Wendell wakes human in the spring thaw, remembering everything, while Mara remembers almost nothing. He chooses to be patient — a wolf at her door, a story told again from the beginning. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope; love as choice renewed daily.
